name: Tibialis Raise
description: Stand with your back against a wall, heels planted a step out from the wall and weight on the heels. Keeping the heels down, pull the toes and the balls of the feet up toward the shins as high as possible, then lower under control. Trains the tibialis anterior (the muscle on the front of the shin) — the antagonist to the calves. Cheap insurance for shin and ankle health, especially for runners, and it builds the dorsiflexion that supports deep squat depth. Can be done bodyweight against a wall, or loaded with a tib bar / plate hooked over the toes.
